verdict.rationale: GitCafe's own docs state that its repositories work with any Git client over HTTPS or SSH. They back this with personal access tokens for Git over HTTPS, a CLI step that configures Git credentials for HTTPS remotes, and default SSH access using keys imported from GitHub. Missing for 10: a dedicated guide to clone/pull/push and SSH key setup, and independent or hands-on corroboration of standard-client interoperability.

support.subject: As a developer, I can clone, pull, and push repositories with any standard Git client over HTTPS or SSH

citations.quote: GitCafe repositories work with any Git client over HTTPS or SSH.
A personal access token lets scripts, CI jobs and tools use the REST API or Git over HTTPS as you, with only the permissions you grant.
`cafe auth http setup` lets Git use it for HTTPS remotes.
Your new account also gets the SSH and GPG keys on your GitHub profile, with the default SSH access
